meta_description: Get in-depth design advice to optimize your plastic parts for injection molding. Designing with moldability in mind can accelerate production time and reduce production costs.
monitored_text: Design for Moldability Toolkit Explore best practices for common molding challenges and learn how thoughtful design decisions can improve manufacturability, reduce costs, and support overall project success. Certification + Compliance ISO 9001:2015 | ISO 13485:2016 | AS9100D | ITAR Optimizing Part Design for Molding Explore practical design guidance to optimize plastic parts for injection molding. Applying proven design for manufacturability (DFM) principles can improve part quality, reduce development risk, and support a smoother path from prototype to production. Designing Complex Features for Molded Parts → Undercuts → Bump-offs → Side-actions → Shut-offs → Core and Cavity → Wall Thickness Navigating Critical Molding Advisories → Insufficient Draft → Gate and Ejector Pin Layout → Radii Added → Non-metal Safe Changes Designing for Moldability See how common injection molding design considerations can impact manufacturability, cost, and production efficiency. This video explores key design principles and practical strategies to help you create better molded parts before production. Injection Molding from Prototyping to Production Meet quality requirements and scale efficiently. Learn how planning for production early can help reduce risk, accelerate product launches, and support long-term manufacturing success. Learn More Designing Complex Features for Molded Parts Undercuts Create complex geometries such as clips, openings, and pass-through features without compromising manufacturability. Learn how cams and inserts can help accommodate undercuts in molded part designs Read Tip Bump-offs Reduce tooling complexity for small undercut features by incorporating bump-offs where geometry and material selection allow. Learn when this approach may be a practical alternative to side-actions. Read Tip Side-actions Incorporate openings, windows, and other undercut features that cannot be formed in a straight-pull mold. Learn how side-actions can expand design flexibility while supporting manufacturability. Read Tip Shut-offs Create complex molded geometries and pass-through features without additional mobile tooling components. Learn how shut-offs can be used to accommodate undercuts and simplify mold construction. Read Tip Core and Cavity Improve manufacturability and part quality with thoughtful core and cavity placement. Learn how mold design decisions can influence appearance, performance, and overall molding outcomes. Read Tip Bosses Well-designed bosses can improve assembly performance while helping reduce sink and other molding challenges. Learn best practices for sizing, draft, wall thickness, and reinforcement to create stronger, more manufacturable parts. See Guidelines Navigating Critical Molding Advisories Draft Needed Improve moldability and support reliable part ejection by incorporating appropriate draft into your design. Learn strategies for applying draft while maintaining critical part features and design intent. See Guidelines arrow_right_alt Gate and Ejector Pin Layout Thoughtful gate and ejector pin placement can influence part quality, cosmetics, and overall molding performance. Learn key considerations for designing parts that support effective filling and ejection. See Guidelines arrow_right_alt Corner Radii Understand how internal corners are formed during mold machining. Learn when radii may be required and how to design for them effectively. See Guidelines arrow_right_alt Wall Thickness Consistent wall thickness is critical to achieving dimensional stability, reducing warpage, and preventing sink. Learn best practices for designing wall sections that support manufacturability, part quality, and overall molding performance. See Guidelines arrow_right_alt Need Help with Your Part Mold Design? Schedule a free design review with on of our applications engineers.
